We have many models in this commit. Are all of these being used in the Sensors page functionality?

Yes (Plus AccountService).  There are 1824 models generated from the latest Redfish openapi.yaml file.
The parent [86518](https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/webui-vue/+/86518) added AccountService but here I updated the pre-commit script to also include *all* dependencies recursively for each model, hence we have a lot of AccountService stuff added here as well.

These are not built in to the image, and are not even needed to compile, they are purely for Typescript IDE/Agent support.  But I thought I would keep the number down and create a script to only commit the models that are currently being used.
Export functionality is not working in Sensors page.
There is a new "Show more" and "Show less" functionality here, Let us keep the original implementation. If needed additional features, let us create a new PR for them.
Search functionality is not working properly with "Show more" and "Show less". If we enter content with "Show more" mode and then move to "Show less" mode. the Table is not updated.

Select all functionality is not working properly
On the first click of Select all checkbox, only one entry is selected
On the second click, all entries are selected

@vedangimittal3004@gmail.com Can you double-check this?  What browser/OS are you using?  I tried Chrome and Firefox on Mac and did not see any issues.  Anything in the Browser console?  Even though we are not going to accept this patch I would like to work out any table issues since we're using Tanstack table here and some new composables.  Did you do a npm install first?

When I searched for a term matching the "Id" column (only visible in expanded mode), then clicked "Show less", the search results didn't update even though the Id column was now hidden.
This is because TanStack Table's global filter was memoized based on the filter string value. When showMore toggled:
- The columns changed (Id column added/removed)
- But the filter string stayed the same
- TanStack returned cached results, ignoring the column change

I moved global filtering from TanStack into the filteredSensors Vue computed, which explicitly depends on columns.value. Now when showMore changes → columns changes → the computed re-evaluates → search results update correctly.
This leverages Vue's reactivity system instead of fighting TanStack's memoization.

I updated the parent [86518](https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/webui-vue/+/86518) so that all of the AccountService model dependencies are included there, removing them from this review after the rebase.  So only Sensor-related models are included.  There are still many models here, but going forward we should see less and less as common base models are added.

Still, this is one of the downsides of this approach:  Updating code with new model imports will create a number of related model Adds to the MR.

Fixed.

The component now uses the Blob URL approach:

- Creates a Blob from the JSON data
- Generates an object URL via URL.createObjectURL()
- Creates a temporary <a> element, triggers click to download
- Cleans up by removing the element and revoking the URL

If you're exporting very large datasets, data URIs can still hit browser limits. I moved to Blob URL approach as it is more robust.  This changes behavior as it shows a "Save as.." dialog.

You're right.  It is a new feature and not fully thought out here.
There are better more common patterns to follow here.
This probably should be a Column Visibility Dropdown; a multi-select dropdown (similar to the existing status filter) where users check which columns to show.
I've updated this in the new patch.

Since we don't plan to commit this PR as-is, I'll leave it in for now so that we can verify the other search-related bug reported here.  (I still wish to dig further using Tanstack table and custom composables to replace the Vue 2 mixins.)
Yes, I ran npm install first and tested on macOS using Firefox. The issue occurs when the Select All checkbox is selected and deselected multiple times.
